title: Homepage voice microspecs & developer pledge
body:
Purpose
This is a compact microspec + experiment plan for homepage and primary product pages focused on a developer-centric voice: authoritative but pragmatic, concise proof points that speak to latency, cost, and operational control. The goal: fast testable variants that communicate the core Redwood differentiation without leaning on competitive name-calling.

Guiding principles (tone + constraints)
- Voice: engineer-first, not marketing-slick. Use plain technical verbs (run, route, optimize) and concrete levers (batching, KV cache, autoscale).
- Brevity: hero headline <= 8 words, subhead <= 20 words. One primary CTA, one secondary.
- Proof: include measurable levers (ms latency ranges, % cost reductions, uptime SLA) when possible.
- Trust: show ops controls and deployment modes as short chips (Hosted • Dedicated • Private).
- Avoid jargon overload: assume reader knows LLM basics but not Redwood specifics.

High-level positioning statement (single sentence)
Redwood Inference: predictable, production-grade LLM serving that lets engineering teams control latency, cost, and availability across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Hero copy experiment matrix
Variant A (control — engineering pledge)
- Headline: "Predictable inference. Built for engineers."
- Subhead: "Ship LLM features with consistent latency, observable costs, and deployment choices: Hosted • Dedicated • Private."
- Primary CTA: "Try for free"
- Secondary CTA: "See performance benchmarks"

Variant B (economics-forward)
- Headline: "Choose latency or cost — or both."
- Subhead: "Autoscale, quantize, and cache to meet your SLOs while minimizing per-token spend."
- Primary CTA: "Estimate my cost"
- Secondary CTA: "Compare configs"

Variant C (ops-first)
- Headline: "Inference that stays online when it matters."
- Subhead: "Fallbacks, rollouts, and region routing to keep customer-facing apps resilient under load."
- Primary CTA: "Request an SLA"
- Secondary CTA: "See routing policies"

Microcopy: developer pledge (short block under hero)
- 3 bullets, micro-commit style, each 6–10 words: 
  • "Per-request latency targets and measurable budgets."
  • "One API, three deployment modes, identical behavior."
  • "Built-in rollouts, canaries, and automatic fallbacks."

Product page hero snippets (Dedicated, Hosted, Private)
- Hosted (short): "Hosted API: instant production access, usage billed per token."
- Dedicated (short): "Dedicated: reserved GPU pools and committed throughput."
- Private (short): "Private: VPC and on-prem options for regulated workloads."

Proof point chips (to appear under hero or as small grid)
- "Median response: 50–150 ms (8k context, x platform)"
- "Average per-token spend reduction: 20–60% with caching + batching"
- "99.95% uptime SLA (Dedicated customers)"
- "Deployments in 3 regions; autoscale in <5 mins"

Micro-UX copy for product pages
- Toggle text for benchmarking: "Show raw token latencies" / "Show 95th-percentile"
- Config CTA: "Open optimizer" (launches Optimize flow)
- Rollout language: "Canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%" (short explanation link)

Competitive framing notes (short bullets for writers and product marketers)
- Competitor X focuses on turnkey simplicity but hides observability; emphasize our token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency dashboards.
- Competitor Y sells cheapest per-token in benchmarks but offers limited fallbacks and no private VPC; stress our graceful degradation and private deployment parity.
- Positioning angle: not "best model" but "best way to serve models reliably and cheaply at scale."

Example single-line comparison blurbs (for small crossheads)
- "More predictable than DIY, more controllable than general-purpose endpoints."
- "Keep app performance stable when traffic spikes — without overprovisioning."

A/B test plan (metrics + success criteria)
- Primary metric: click-through to sign-up or cost estimator (CTR). Secondary: time-on-page, benchmark sheet downloads, sign-up conversion.
- Variant success threshold: +8% CTR and +5% signups at p<0.05 over 14 days.
- Segmentation: organic developer traffic, paid trial traffic, docs-to-site referrers.

Landing QA / content checklist before pushing live
- Headlines are <= 8 words. Subheads <= 20 words.
- Chips: no more than 4 proof chips visible above the fold.
- Benchmarks link opens a non-gated PDF.
- All internal links point to correct product docs (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).
- Mobile: hero stacks headline -> subhead -> pledge -> CTAs; CTAs both visible on first fold.

Copy dos and don’ts (quick)
- Do: use concrete levers (cache, batch, quantize), numbers when available, and short present-tense verbs.
- Don’t: call out competitors by name, overpromise unattainable latency targets, or bury the CTA in long paragraphs.

Suggested short CTAs (prioritized)
- "Try for free" (primary, for product-led flows)
- "Estimate my cost" (developer-calculator funnel)
- "Request an SLA" (enterprise-assisted flows)
- "See benchmarks" (proof-focused, non-gated)

Localization notes
- Keep hero text compact to simplify translations. Avoid idioms.
- For EU/APAC region pages, swap region-specific proofs (e.g., local region list, data residency note) higher on the page.

Next steps & ownership
- Design: produce three hero comps (A/B/C) by 2026-02-16 — owner: Asha.
- Frontend: implement experiment flags and tracking — owner: Miguel; ticket: JIRA:GTM-5472.
- Growth: schedule 2-week paid/organic test window once experiment is live — owner: Tomás.
- Content: incorporate comms checklist and finalize microcopy by 2026-02-24 — owner: Claire.

Appendix: quick variants (for use in small components)
- Micro-hero alternatives (very short):
  • "Serve LLMs with predictable cost."
  • "Inference engineered for production."
  • "Latency guarantees, without the ops overhead."

- One-liners for social and ads (<=120 characters):
  • "Control latency, costs, and deployment — with one API."
  • "From prototype to scale: inference that won’t surprise you."

Notes and unresolved questions (to surface in sync)
- Request engineering: can we reliably publish median response ranges per model variant? Action: product/infra feasibility check due 2026-02-14.
- Legal: any constraints on publishing per-token cost ranges in advertised materials? Action: legal review by 2026-02-18.

This doc is intended as a working spec. Please add comments inline or ping the linked Slack thread for quick synchronizations.
